subject: Copywriting
title: The PS Line Secret
description: A quick win: understand The PS Line Secret.

hook.text: Eye-tracking studies show the PS line is the second-most-read part of an email, right after the subject line.

buildup.text: The PS was a necessity in typed letters—corrections added at the bottom. In email, it's a strategic weapon.

discovery.text: Direct response marketers load the PS with urgency, bonuses, or a restatement of the core benefit.

twist.text: A PS works because it looks personal and afterthought-like. The reader's guard drops. It feels less like selling.

climax.text: Test a strong PS in your next email: restate the offer, add a deadline, or reveal a bonus. Watch clicks jump.

punchline.text: The PS is the second-most-read line. Use it to close the deal.

quiz.question: What is the most-read part of an email after the subject line?

details.summary: The PS (postscript) line is the second-most-read element in any email after the subject line. Eye-tracking studies show readers jump to the PS before reading body copy. Smart email writers use the PS to restate the key benefit, add urgency, or include a personal aside that reinforces the main...
details.whyItMatters: The PS is prime real estate that most email writers waste or skip entirely. Knowing that readers gravitate to it provides a powerful tactical advantage for reinforcing your core message.
takeaways: Eye-tracking shows the PS is the second-most-read element in email
Use the PS to restate the key offer or add urgency
A personal PS creates intimacy in otherwise formal marketing emails

faq.question: Why do people read the PS line before the body?
faq.answer: Readers scan emails for the most dense, actionable information. The PS stands out visually as a separate section and signals a summary or bonus. In direct mail tradition, the PS was where you put your best shot because readers always looked there first.

faq.question: What should you write in a PS line?
faq.answer: Restate your main benefit or offer, add a time-sensitive incentive, or share a personal note that builds connection. The PS works best when it gives readers a reason to scroll back up and read the full email or click the CTA they skipped.
